extracted.intended_audience: SBIR/STTR applicants (small businesses) preparing NIH/NIAID R43/R44 grant applications for diagnostic devices
extracted.subtask_description: A sample NIH SBIR (R44) application for a point-of-care HIV antigen/antibody diagnostic device, including required forms (SF424/PHS398), project narrative, biosketches, facilities/equipment, human subjects protections, and related attachments. Useful as a template and source of procedural and compliance requirements for preparing a similar application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow FOA/application instructions for format
rubrics_metrics.description: Always follow your funding opportunity's instructions for application format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although this application demonstrates good grantsmanship, time has passed since the grantee applied. The samples may not reflect the latest format or rules. NIAID posts new samples periodically: https://www.niaid.nih.gov/grants-contracts/sample_applications

rubrics_metrics.name: SF 424 (R&R) and Required Face Page Fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide all required SF424 (R&R) face page information: type of submission, applicant organizational DUNS, legal name, address, EIN/TIN, type of applicant, project title, dates, PI contact information, congressional district, and other required fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sample shows required fields and how they are presented; applicants must complete the SF424 (R&R) and related mandatory data elements exactly as required by the FOA/system.

rubrics_metrics.name: PHS 398 Specific Components (Project Summary/Abstract and Public Health Relevance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a Project Summary/Abstract (Description) and a Public Health Relevance Statement (Narrative attachment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Project Summary should concisely state goals and outcomes (e.g., develop low-cost POC HIV Ag/Ab device). Public Health Relevance should state how the proposal addresses an unmet need and potential public health impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table of Contents and Required Attachments
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a complete table of contents listing SF424 R&R and PHS-398 specific attachments (e.g., Project Summary, Facilities & Resources, Equipment, Biographical Sketches, Budget, Research Plan, Human Subjects sections).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize the application with page numbers and attachments as demonstrated; include all required components referenced in the FOA and forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Aims
rubrics_metrics.description: State clear Specific Aims for the project (concise, numbered aims describing intended technical milestones and objectives).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example aims: combine antigen detection with multiplexed serology assay, modify cartridge/reader/software for automated result and CLIA waiver guidance, validate with well-characterized specimen panels, capture operational/usability feedback and preliminary whole blood dataset for IDE meeting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Strategy / Approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a detailed Research Strategy describing methods, assay selection, optimization, validation plans, and milestones to achieve aims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain assay pair selection, antigen choices, reagent conjugations, cross-reactivity testing, minimization of assay steps, heat-stable reagent formulation, automation of reader/software, and validation sample sizes and composition (e.g., numbers of acute/seropositive/negative specimens).

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilities & Other Resources — Description and Adequacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe organizational facilities, lab spaces, controlled-access areas, staffing, and administrative support to demonstrate capacity to perform the proposed work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include facility square footage, dedicated lab areas (assay wet lab, BL2 laboratory, PCR labs, instrument lab, cleanroom, cartridge development area), staffing roles (R&D, G&A, regulatory), and access to institutional resources; show that facilities meet biosafety and operational needs for the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biosafety and Biocontainment Compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Facilities that handle human samples must meet relevant biosafety guidance (e.g., operate a Biosafety Level 2 Laboratory designed per BMBL 5th Edition).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document use of certified industrial hygiene experts for annual training, safety audits, plan reviews; compliance with OSHA Bloodborne Pathogen training and vaccination requirements; and procedures for biological waste management via a certified hauler.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laboratory Organization to Prevent Contamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Design laboratory workflow and spatial separation to prevent contamination (e.g., separate pre-PCR, PCR, and post-PCR stations; unidirectional traffic flow).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe HEPA-filtered hoods, UV-equipped forced-air hoods, dedicated refrigerators/freezers/pipettes per PCR station, and other contamination-control practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equipment — Availability and Appropriateness
rubrics_metrics.description: List and document access to major equipment required for the project (e.g., biosafety cabinets, centrifuges, thermal cyclers, microscopes, environmental chambers, packaging/assembly equipment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide equipment organized by location and show that equipment supports planned assays, instrument development, cartridge assembly, and stability testing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cartridge/Device Development and Stability Testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe dedicated workspace and equipment for disposable cartridge development and stability testing (e.g., environmental chambers with humidity control, heat sealers, plasma ovens, contact angle measurement tools).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include methods for controlled flowrate development, heat-stability formulation, and use of environmental chambers for accelerated stability and shelf-life studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biographical Sketch Content and Length
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a biographical sketch for each senior/key person including name, position title, eRA commons user name, education/training, personal statement, positions and honors, selected publications, and research support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow PHS 398 format and DO NOT EXCEED FOUR PAGES per biographical sketch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human Subjects Involvement — Protocols and Approvals
rubrics_metrics.description: If human subjects are involved, describe protections, potential risks, recruitment, consent processes, and obtain IRB approval and Human Subject Assurance numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State whether human subjects are involved, provide IRB approval dates if available, and ensure local IRB/Ethics Committee approval before recruitment; include details on sample handling and consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection Against Risks / Confidentiality Measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe adequacy of protection against risks including confidentiality procedures (e.g., coding of records, secure storage, limited access to master linkage).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detail how research records identify participants only by coded numbers, where master linkage is stored and who has access, and plans to limit psychological/social risks (e.g., inadvertent disclosure).

rubrics_metrics.name: Informed Consent Procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide detailed informed consent procedures including translation/back-translation, verbal discussions, documentation, alternatives, risks/benefits, compensation, and record-keeping.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consent must comply with local IRB/ethics guidelines; if participants cannot read, follow local guidance for consent; signed consents retained in medical record and study site source document; participant receives a copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential Risks and Benefits — Disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicitly state potential physical, psychological, and social risks of participation (e.g., venipuncture risks, possible psychological trauma from diagnosis) and potential benefits to subjects and public health.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include statement that risks are minimal where appropriate, alternatives to participation, and describe possible benefit such as earlier diagnosis leading to treatment/referral and public health impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data and Safety Monitoring Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a plan to monitor data integrity and safety, including adverse event monitoring and reporting processes, and oversight mechanisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor at institution level for adverse events; report events per institutional policy; use conference calls and face-to-face meetings to monitor data collection and integrity; include NIH project officers in monitoring when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of Women and Minorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Address inclusion of women and racial/ethnic minorities in study populations and plans to analyze potential differences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure representation reflects local epidemiology; state that any sex or racial/ethnic differences will be explored in secondary analyses where sample sizes allow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of Children — Justification
rubrics_metrics.description: State whether children will be included and justify exclusion or inclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If children are excluded, provide rationale (e.g., inability to provide independent consent, sample quality); indicate plans for future inclusion in later phases if assay proves sensitive and specific.

rubrics_metrics.name: Planned Enrollment Table and Demographic Reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a Planned Enrollment Table with number of subjects by ethnic category, sex/gender, and racial categories; ensure totals match (Ethnic Category total must equal Racial Categories total).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report targeted/planned enrollment numerically and ensure consistency across tables (example: total planned enrollment = 100 with breakdown by Hispanic/Not Hispanic and race).

rubrics_metrics.name: IRB/IACUC and Regulatory Compliance Items
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose IRB/IACUC approval status, animal use, environmental impact questions, proprietary information, and foreign activities per the Other Project Information form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answer required yes/no questions on human subjects, animal use, environmental impact, foreign collaborations; provide explanations or attachments where needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventions, Patents, and Intellectual Property Disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Respond to PHS 398 checklist items on inventions and patents (renewal applications must list inventions/patents previously reported).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If 'Yes,' provide details in the specified format; ensure disclosure per FOA and institutional policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program Income and Financial Disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: If program income is anticipated, document anticipated amounts and sources for each budget period on the PHS 398 Checklist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answer 'Is program income anticipated?' and, if yes, provide amounts and sources using the format in the checklist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure Permission Statement for Unfunded Applications
rubrics_metrics.description: State whether the government is permitted to disclose the project title and applicant contact information to organizations interested in potential collaborations or investment if the application is not funded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete the PHS 398 Checklist question regarding disclosure permission (Yes/No).

rubrics_metrics.name: Document and Attachment Management
rubrics_metrics.description: Include and label required attachments (e.g., Project Summary, Project Narrative, Bibliography, Facilities, Equipment, Biographical Sketches, Budget Justification) and ensure they are viewable/attached in the submission system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the application system's attach/delete/view functionality correctly; include the referenced supporting documents and ensure file names and attachments match table of contents entries.
